description: What the main window may do. It has no network of its own and never holds a token: its requests to the site's API go out from Rust, which checks the address and attaches the token of the session the page names (api_request, and api_abort to stop one: api.rs). Links open in the browser, http(s) only. The window starts hidden and Rust shows it once the page says it has drawn (page_ready), unless the app started at login with --hidden, so the page gets no show or set-focus; Start at login is the autostart plugin's enable, disable and is-enabled; the networks signed in to are listed and switched in Rust (list_sessions, switch_session: a request only ever carries the token of the network it was made for), and the active network whose sign-in kept no name (an older version's) gets the one its site gives (name_network: only an empty name, only the active one's); a request the site answers 401 renews that session in Rust at once, or keeps it in the list as signed out, never forgets it, and the page asks how the session stands (token_refused); una:// links reach the page through take_deep_links, never the deep-link plugin's own commands; the menu's Back and Forward follow the page's history and File > New Post says New Task where Cmd+N adds a task to the list shown (set_nav_state) and its sidebar item says what Cmd+\ does next, Show Icons Only or Show Sidebar Names (set_sidebar_shown); the page asks which material its sidebar is drawn over (window_material, material.rs) and names the window after what it shows (set-title: the Window menu, Mission Control and screen readers read it); the network, profile and resize-handle menus are native pop-up menus that Rust builds from the items the page sends (popup_menu, popup.rs), so the page needs no menu permission; the theme chosen in the app (light, dark or the system's) goes to the window too (set-theme), so the title bar and background match; on macOS the page draws the title bar, so its headers drag the window (start-dragging, and internal-toggle-maximize for a double click). OS notifications, the tray and the badge are Rust's (sync.rs, tray.rs, badge.rs): the page gets no notification, tray or badge permission, only the sync events. Copy Link writes text with the clipboard plugin (write-text only: the page never reads the clipboard). Deletes are confirmed with the dialog plugin's ask(), which is its message command: no file open or save dialogs (the photo picker for uploads opens from Rust, upload.rs, and the page gets a handle, never a path); a file downloaded from the network (a Files entry's download_url) is saved by Rust too (save_download, download.rs): Rust opens the save dialog and writes the file where the person chose, so the page gets no save dialog or file system permission. Lasting drafts are the store plugin's drafts.json, which Rust opens at start (lib.rs): the page may look up a store already open (get-store) and read, write, delete, list and save it, but never load one by path, which would reach any file. Settings are not a store: Rust keeps them (settings.rs) and the page reads them with get_settings and changes them with set_setting, which only this window gets. Of the core permissions only what the page uses (events it listens to, its window and web view, resources), not core:default: the tray and the menu are built in Rust, so the page gets no tray or menu permission, and it sends no events (no emit). Live events from the network's sockets server come from Rust too (realtime.rs): the page names the public channels it wants (realtime_watch, checked there) and hears their events, ids only, as the realtime event; it opens no WebSocket of its own. New versions: the page asks Rust whether there is one (check_update) and to install the one found (install_update, only after the person chose Install and Restart: updater.rs); it gets no permission of the updater or process plugins, so it can name no other address, package or key, and cannot restart the app itself. The app's own commands are granted one by one (build.rs lists them): the main window gets all of them, open_window included (windows.rs); windows of their own get capabilities/secondary.json.
